Women's share of the workforce, by sector
Women's share of workforceAll companies (18%)
18%Women, NSE workforce
1,372Companies reporting

Women are 18% of the workforce across the 1,372 NSE-listed companies that reported gender data in FY 2025–26, almost unchanged from two years earlier. Representation ranges from 49% in Hospitals and Labs to 2% in Construction.

Sector-wise breakdown Formal workforce (BRSR) Gender representation
Go to dashboard

Wide sector spread

Women are 49% of the workforce in Hospitals and Labs but just 2% in Construction.

Heavy industry lags

In 10 of 24 sectors, women are under 10% of the workforce, including Power, Chemicals, Metals and Mining, and Capital Goods.

Few sectors above average

Only 6 of 24 sectors are above the 18% all-company average, led by Hospitals and Labs, Textiles, Consumer Services and IT.

State-wise map Employment type breakdown Rural / urban split
Go to dashboard

Employment type mix

Self-employment accounts for 55% of all work, ahead of regular-wage jobs (25%) and casual labour (20%).

Contract status

57% of women in regular-wage jobs have no written contract, similar to 58% across all regular-wage workers.

Women's share by state

Among larger states, women's share of the workforce ranges from 40% in Chhattisgarh to 14% in Delhi.

Sources: TUF merged manufacturing directory (Sep 2026); OpenStreetMap highways. 23 of 108 unit locations are manual map pins. Villages counted if any part touches a buffer.

Highway access

The clusters' 5 km areas are crossed by 13 highway and expressway routes. Five pass through the area around Khopoli–Khalapur, including the Mumbai–Pune Expressway.

Proximity to Skilling Opportunities

Only 1 of 18 mapped ITIs lies within a cluster buffer — ITI Khalapur. Most training capacity sits outside the 5 km catchments.

Village catchments

243 villages touch a buffer and 113 lie fully inside one. Dolvi–Pen reaches the most villages (59) with just three mapped units.

Women's share of net EPF subscribers added, by fiscal year *2025–26 is a partial year
21.0%Women's share of net subscribers added, Jul 2025
28.6%Women's share of new subscribers, Jul 2025

Women make up about one in five net additions to EPF, a share that has stayed between 18% and 22% every year since FY 2020–21.

Monthly updates Age groups Sectors
Go to dashboard

Faster growth, flat share

Net EPF additions rose 40% for women and 33% for men between FY 2023–24 and FY 2024–25, yet women's share moved only from 19.7% to 20.5%.

Women join later

Most new male subscribers join at 18–21; most new female subscribers join at 22–25.

Fewer women return

In July 2025, women were 28.6% of new subscribers but only 17.3% of those who rejoined EPF after leaving.

Women-specific provisions in startup policies, by state and UT (score 0–6)

Hover or tap a state to see which types of support its policy offers women founders.

Types of support offered06

Six types of support assessed

  1. FiscalGrants, allowances, subsidies and funding preferences
  2. InfrastructureIncubation seats, women-focused incubators, co-working space, plots
  3. RegulatoryWomen-specific rules and market access, incl. procurement preferences
  4. UpskillingTraining, mentoring and acceleration programmes
  5. GovernanceA dedicated women's mission, wing or centre
  6. AdditionalAwards, networking events and ecosystem commitments
30 of 36States & UTs with a provision
1State covers all six (Tamil Nadu)

30 of 36 states and UTs explicitly provide for women-led startups in their startup policy, with at least one provision over and above what all startups receive.

State map Six provision types State policy pages
Go to dashboard

Policy priorities

25 of 36 states and UTs offer women founders fiscal support, such as grants or allowances. Only 4 provide for a dedicated institution, such as a women's mission or cell.

Thin coverage

23 of 36 states and UTs offer women-led startups at most one of the six types of support. Only Tamil Nadu (all six) and Nagaland (five) cover five or more.

Large startup states

Four of the five states with the most women-led startups offer three or more types of support.
